name: West Florida Public Libraries (Pensacola Main Library)
notes: Flagship central library branch in downtown Pensacola with active cultural programs.

name: WFPL Tryon Branch Library
notes: Uptown Pensacola branch on Langley Avenue hosting weekly family storytimes and maker workshops.

name: WFPL Southwest Branch Library
notes: Southwest branch serving Perdido and Warrington neighborhoods on Gulf Beach Highway.

name: WFPL Westside Branch Library
notes: Westside Pensacola library on US 90 offering adult digital literacy and youth robotics programs.

name: WFPL Bellview Library
notes: Modern Bellview community branch with dedicated teen center and outdoor reading garden.

name: WFPL Molino Branch Library
notes: Located in the historic Molino schoolhouse community complex with local agricultural history talks.

name: WFPL Century Branch Library
notes: Northern Escambia County branch serving Century and Flomaton border residents.

name: WFPL West Florida Genealogy Library
notes: Specialized genealogical and local archival collection located in historic North Spring Street district.

name: City of Pensacola Municipal & Community Council Meetings
notes: Official city hall calendar for City Council, Planning Board, and citizen task force hearings.

name: Town of Century Council & Community Gatherings
notes: Municipal council meetings and community clean-up assemblies at Century Town Hall.

name: Saenger Theatre Pensacola
notes: Historic 1925 Spanish Baroque theatre on Intendencia St hosting Broadway tours, orchestra, and comedy.

name: Pensacola Little Theatre & Cultural Center
notes: Belmont-DeVilliers adjacent premier community theater with mainstage dramas, musicals, and youth academy.

name: Pensacola Opera Mainstage & Pop-Up Operas
notes: Professional regional opera company producing grand opera at the Saenger and free community Songbird pop-ups.

name: Pensacola Symphony Orchestra
notes: The region foremost professional symphony performing Masterworks, Pops, and free chamber concerts.

name: Ballet Pensacola
notes: Resident dance company presenting classical and contemporary ballets at Pensacola Cultural Center.

name: Choral Society of Pensacola
notes: 100-voice symphonic chorus performing major choral works and annual Messiah in historic venues.

name: Jazz Pensacola Live Concerts & Jams
notes: Nonprofit presenting monthly Jazz Gumbo concerts, student jazz competitions, and annual JazzFest.

name: Bands on the Beach (Pensacola Beach Gulfside Pavilion)
notes: Tuesday evening free outdoor sunset concert series from April through October on the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Pensacola Museum of Art (PMA / UWF)
notes: Located in the historic 1906 Spanish Revival city jail, featuring rotating 20th-century and contemporary exhibitions.

name: First City Art Center (FCAC)
notes: Grassroots working arts center offering glassblowing hot shop, pottery studio, and monthly Hot Glass Cold Brew.

name: Gallery Night Pensacola
notes: Monthly 3rd Friday evening arts takeover closing 10 blocks of Palafox Street for 50+ local artists and buskers.

name: The Art Gallery (TAG) at UWF
notes: Center for Fine and Performing Arts gallery presenting regional contemporary art and BFA exit exhibitions.

name: Anna Lamar Switzer Center for Visual Arts (PSC)
notes: Pensacola State College premiere visual arts complex hosting visiting national masters and permanent collection.

name: Quayside Art Gallery (Pensacola Artists Inc)
notes: The largest co-op art gallery in the Southeast, founded in 1973 in a historic 1873 building on Plaza Ferdinand.

name: Blue Morning Gallery
notes: Artist-owned cooperative gallery on South Palafox showcasing photography, fused glass, and Gulf Coast paintings.

name: Historic Pensacola Village (UWF Historic Trust)
notes: Preserves 8.5 acres of downtown history with 28 properties including TT Wentworth Museum and Old Christ Church.

name: National Naval Aviation Museum (NAS Pensacola)
notes: One of the world largest aviation museums with 150 restored aircraft and Blue Angels flight practice viewing.

name: Pensacola Lighthouse & Maritime Museum
notes: 1859 historic beacon across from NAS Pensacola offering 177-step tower climbs and sunset ghost tours.

name: Pensacola Museum of History (T.T. Wentworth Jr)
notes: Three-story Mediterranean Revival 1907 City Hall housing premier Gulf Coast historical collections.

name: General Daniel "Chappie" James Jr. Museum & Flight Academy
notes: Birthplace home of the first African American four-star general in United States military history.

name: UWF Archaeology Institute & Public Labs
notes: Research facility discovering Tristan de Luna 1559 Spanish shipwreck fleet and Native American sites.

name: Pensacola African American Heritage Society
notes: Leading historic walking tours of Belmont-DeVilliers and African American civil rights landmarks.

name: Gulf Islands National Seashore - Fort Pickens Ranger Programs
notes: Pristine barrier island dunes, brick battery tours, night sky astronomy, and coastal bird walks.

name: Big Lagoon State Park
notes: Gateway to the Florida Circumnavigational Saltwater Paddling Trail, bird observation tower, and salt flats.

name: Perdido Key State Park
notes: White sand barrier island protecting nesting sea turtles and the endangered Perdido Key beach mouse.

name: Tarkiln Bayou Preserve State Park
notes: Home to four species of rare carnivorous pitcher plants and boardwalks through wet prairie savannahs.

name: Bayview Park & Bayou Texar Waterfront
notes: Pensacola premier community waterfront park with kayak launch, dog beach, and outdoor fitness.

name: Vince J. Whibbs Sr. Community Maritime Park
notes: Vibrant bayfront public amphitheater and green lawn adjacent to Blue Wahoos Stadium.

name: University of West Florida Events
notes: UWF master university Localist calendar for public lectures, symposiums, and campus assemblies.

name: UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts (CFPA)
notes: Main stage for university student opera, symphonic wind ensemble, jazz band, and theater productions.

name: UWF Hal Marcus College of Science & Engineering Forums
notes: Public research presentations in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, and marine biology.

name: Pensacola State College Ashmore Auditorium
notes: 1,200-seat premier performing arts center on Pensacola 9th Avenue campus hosting college arts season.

name: Pensacola State College Planetarium & Space Theater
notes: 40-foot dome digital projection theater featuring live star talks, telescope viewings, and space exploration shows.

name: UF/IFAS Extension Escambia County
notes: Florida Master Gardener training, 4-H livestock exhibitions, and sustainable landscaping seminars.

name: Flora-Bama Lounge & Oyster Bar
notes: Legendary honky-tonk straddling the Florida-Alabama line; 5 stages of live country, rock, and Americana daily.

name: Seville Quarter Historic Entertainment Complex
notes: Iconic 1870s historic district complex with 7 rooms including Rosie O'Grady's Dueling Pianos and Phineas Phogg's.

name: Vinyl Music Hall
notes: Historic Palafox street indoor concert hall hosting national touring rock, indie, electronic, and metal acts.

name: The Handlebar (Historic Punk & Indie Venue)
notes: Historic subterranean rock and punk club hosting local underground bands and touring indie musicians.

name: Emerald Republic Brewing Co
notes: Downtown craft brewery with expansive outdoor beer garden hosting local acoustic jams, comedy, and vinyl DJ nights.

name: Paradise Bar & Grill (Pensacola Beach Santa Rosa Sound)
notes: Open-air soundside tiki bar hosting regional blues, rock, and reggae bands directly on the water.

name: Pensacola MESS Hall (Math, Engineering, Science & Stuff)
notes: Hands-on discovery science museum in downtown Pensacola where visitors engage in real scientific investigation.

name: Pensacola Children's Museum (UWF Historic Trust)
notes: Multi-level hands-on children museum exploring Pensacola multicultural colonial heritage through play.

name: Open Books Bookstore & Prison Book Project
notes: Volunteer-run nonprofit bookstore hosting poetry open mics, children reading circles, and community organizing.

name: 309 Punk Project (Archive & Community House)
notes: The oldest continuously operating punk communal house in the South; artist-in-residence workshops and DIY zine fests.

name: Belmont-DeVilliers Cultural Heritage Center
notes: Historic Black commercial district known as "The Blocks", showcasing Chitlin' Circuit history and gospel showcases.

name: Palafox Market
notes: Weekly award-winning Saturday farmers and artisan market closing Palafox Street from 9am-2pm.

name: Palafox Market South (Plaza Ferdinand)
notes: Expanded southern district of Palafox Market around historic Plaza Ferdinand offering local seafood and baked goods.

name: Pensacola Seafood Festival (Fiesta Pensacola)
notes: Annual autumn celebration in Seville Square featuring grilled Gulf grouper, crawfish tails, and 170 craft artisans.

name: Pensacola Crawfish Festival
notes: Spring festival boiling 16,000 lbs of fresh Louisiana crawfish with live Zydeco music at Community Maritime Park.

name: Joe Patti's Seafood Market Heritage Days
notes: Historic seafood institution operating on Pensacola Bay since 1931, offering cooking demos and seafood talks.

name: IHMC - Florida Institute for Human & Machine Cognition
notes: World-leading AI and humanoid robotics research institute in downtown Pensacola hosting acclaimed evening lectures.

name: Blue Angels Flight Demonstrations & Practices
notes: U.S. Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron weekly flight practices viewable from the National Naval Aviation Museum.

name: Florida Cybersecurity Training Center & UWF Center for Cybersecurity
notes: National Center of Academic Excellence hosting NSA and military cybersecurity symposiums.

name: Gulf Coast Technology Council Networking
notes: Monthly meetups bringing together regional defense contractors, software engineers, and IT founders.
